description: The kernel corpus records one iex> call per doc example, and Elixir mode is not an independent oracle (both backends share the builtin typing). Freeze under test/stability/<version>/kernels/ a sample of the test suite's own kernels at the tag with recorded inputs and native outputs: pick kernels that cover each builtin and construct at its edges (overflow boundaries, index errors, non-finite floats, u64, bitstrings, early exit, multi-clause, raise), from test/*_test.exs at v0.1.0, and record for each a handful of calls with the results the tag's code gives (a value, or an exception module with its agreement reason). Reuse the frozen-file form (a module block followed by an iex> block with the recorded results) so the existing freeze task, support module and test read them; extend the freeze task with a list of {test file, kernel module, calls} to freeze, or a generator that evaluates the calls at the tag, so a release freezes them by one command. Keep it fast: stable module names, build cache; report the cold and warm timing. Done when the sample is committed, mix ci passes, and a deliberate change to one builtin's edge behaviour (e.g. the overflow check) fails the new files (tried locally, not committed).

comments.text: PR #16 opened: https://github.com/DanielLuning/defk/pull/16 - the test sample (11 modules, 102 kernels, 302 calls) frozen under test/stability/0.1.0/kernels/test-*.md from the tag; dev/stability/sample.exs lists it, dev/stability/eval.exs runs it at the tag; mix ci passed; two break checks failed the new files as expected. Ticket stays in progress until the owner merges.

title: Stability: freeze a sample of the test suite's kernels with recorded inputs and outputs
